title: Solve SAT Boundaries Questions in the Fastest Order
description: Use a fixed full stop, colon, dash, and comma order to solve SAT Boundaries questions quickly and avoid punctuation traps.

questions.stem_html: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.stimulus_html: The lawn was covered in ______ grounds crew delayed the morning game.
questions.explanation_html: Both ideas can stand as complete sentences. The period is the only offered mark that separates them correctly.
questions.variation: Choose a valid full-stop boundary between independent clauses

distractor_notes.B: Uses only a comma to join independent clauses.
distractor_notes.C: Omits the boundary between complete thoughts.
distractor_notes.D: Uses only a comma to join independent clauses.

questions.stem_html: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.stimulus_html: The campsite faced one practical ______ a ban on open fires during the dry season.
questions.explanation_html: The text before the blank is a complete statement. The ending specifies what that statement anticipates, so a colon introduces the explanation.
questions.variation: Introduce an explanation after a complete thought

distractor_notes.A: Requires a complete independent clause on the right.
distractor_notes.B: Adds a conjunction where the ending does not contain a full clause.
distractor_notes.C: Leaves the explanation without a boundary.
